next_round_constraints: Prioritize structures with an explicit hospitalization compartment (SEIHR or related) and keep observation_map focused on H (avoid I+H mixtures unless strongly justified).
Explore small, discrete reporting/admission delays around hospitalization mapping (delay_weeks ∈ {0,1,2}) but do not rely on delay alone to explain dynamics.
Control instability: prefer specs expected to be robust across rolling splits (avoid adding reinfection/waning unless it demonstrably stabilizes rather than increases variance).
Keep complexity increases minimal and targeted (one additional compartment or one additional mechanism at a time) to avoid penalty-driven regressions.
observed_failure_modes: Delay-only observation (delayed_I with 1–2 week lag) appears insufficient to match hospitalization-rate dynamics; suggests missing explicit hospitalization compartment or mapping mismatch.

SEIRS with delayed_I shows a large gap between single validation vs rolling validation and elevated rolling variability, indicating sensitivity to split/initialization and potential overfitting to the held-out window rather than stable dynamics.
High peakiness likely not well captured by smooth latent-infection observation alone; models without an explicit H state may under/over-shoot peaks depending on lag choice.

Adding complexity (SEIHR) improves rolling behavior relative to SEIR, but some configurations (I+H observation) degrade fit, suggesting observation-map identifiability issues when mixing states directly.
feedback.proposer_instruction: For the next round, propose a tight set of SEIHR-family templates that map observations primarily to H (hospitalizations), optionally with a small delay (0–2 weeks). Avoid combined observation maps like I+H for now. If you include waning/reinfection (SEIRS-like), only do so paired with an H observation and justify it as improving split-to-split stability for high-peak series; otherwise keep to SEIHR with simple, identifiable observation mappings.
